A manager can set status='paid' to mark any payment as paid without processing payment, or set status='overdue' to trigger late-fee assessments, bypassing the entire payment lifecycle.

extra.message: Insecure database connection — no SSL/TLS for PostgreSQL

metadata.proof: SOURCE: default database URL 'postgresql://...' without sslmode parameter → SINK: SQLAlchemy engine. The default connection string has no SSL parameters. When the URL is configured for a remote database (via .env), all data including user passwords, payment records, and PII is transmitted in cleartext, enabling passive eavesdropping and active MitM attacks on the database connection.

extra.message: No rate limiting on CSV import endpoints — unbounded resource consumption

metadata.proof: SOURCE: authenticated user sends unlimited file upload requests → SINK: each request triggers file I/O, CSV parsing, and database writes. All three import endpoints (/tenants at line 29, /units at line 70, /payments at line 103) lack request rate limiting. An attacker with valid manager credentials could upload hundreds of large CSV files simultaneously, exhausting database connections, disk space, and worker threads.

extra.message: User enumeration via distinguishable error response on registration

metadata.proof: SOURCE: user-supplied email in UserCreate request body → SINK: HTTP 400 response with 'Email already registered' message. The endpoint returns different HTTP status codes (400 vs 201) and different response bodies depending on whether the email exists. An attacker can enumerate valid registered emails by observing the distinguishable responses, with no rate limiting to prevent mass enumeration.

extra.message: Logout deletes cookie without matching Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite attributes

metadata.proof: SOURCE: logout endpoint → SINK: response.delete_cookie. The cookie was set with httponly=True and samesite='lax' at line 38-43, but delete_cookie at line 55 omits these attributes. Browsers may fail to delete a cookie when the deletion attributes don't match the original cookie's attributes, leaving the session token valid on the client after logout and enabling session persistence.

extra.message: Cross-property internal note leak — PropertyManager can read all internal notes

metadata.proof: SOURCE: list_messages query filter for PROPERTY_MANAGER role → SINK: Message query result set. The filter condition (Message.is_internal_note == True) at line 44 has no property-scope restriction. A PropertyManager assigned to Property A can view all internal notes across the entire system, including confidential inter-staff communications between admin and managers of Property B, since internal_note messages bypass the tenant/property scoping entirely.

extra.message: Auto database schema creation on every application startup — dangerous in production

metadata.proof: SOURCE: application startup sequence → SINK: SQLAlchemy create_all() call. The code unconditionally creates all database tables on every startup with no environment guard. The comment acknowledges it is 'for dev convenience'. In production this can cause unintended schema modifications, race conditions with concurrent migrations, or startup failures if the DB user lacks DDL permissions, potentially leading to data loss or downtime.

extra.message: Demo account passwords printed to console

metadata.proof: SOURCE: seed.py prints all demo credentials at lines 337-341 to stdout. SINK: these passwords appear in stdout/stderr, which may be captured by CI systems, container orchestration logs (Docker, Kubernetes), or monitoring pipelines. Anyone with access to build or deployment logs obtains valid login credentials for the admin, manager, worker, and tenant accounts in the seeded database.

extra.message: PropertyManager can enumerate all maintenance workers across all properties

metadata.proof: SOURCE: the list_users filter for PROPERTY_MANAGER role at line 46. SINK: the OR condition (User.role == UserRole.MAINTENANCE_WORKER) adds ALL maintenance workers regardless of property assignment. A PropertyManager of Property A can list every maintenance worker in the system, including their emails, full names, and phone numbers, even workers exclusively assigned to Property B that the manager has no legitimate relationship with.

extra.message: Unbounded memory allocation in list_leases — all leases loaded into memory without pagination

metadata.proof: SOURCE: GET /api/leases with no pagination limit. SINK: query.all() loads every matching Lease row (plus joined Tenant and Unit relationships via the response model) into memory at once. An attacker with property_manager role can create thousands of leases, then call list_leases to exhaust server memory, causing denial of service.

extra.message: Unbounded memory allocation in list_inspections — all inspections loaded into memory without pagination

metadata.proof: SOURCE: GET /api/inspections with no pagination limit. SINK: query.all() loads all Inspection rows (plus Unit, Building, Property, and Inspector relationships via the response model) into memory. Combined with mass inspection creation, this can exhaust server memory.

extra.message: IDOR in create_inspection — PropertyManager can set inspector_id to any user across properties

metadata.proof: SOURCE: InspectionCreate schema includes inspector_id (int, required) at schemas.py:282. extra.message: Missing MAINTENANCE_WORKER branch in can_view_inspection — workers silently denied access to individual inspections

metadata.proof: SOURCE: can_view_inspection is called by get_inspection, update_inspection, upload_inspection_photo, and list_inspection_photos at inspections.py. SINK: the function at lines 125-134 has branches for admin, manager, and tenant roles but no branch for MAINTENANCE_WORKER, falling through to return False at line 133. Workers who can see inspections in their list (via the separate worker filter at inspections.py:41-45) can never view, update, or add photos to a specific inspection because can_view_inspection returns False unconditionally for workers. This is a broken access control gap.
